gaps.topic: High-purity quartz → fused-quartz crucible makers → wafer makers
gaps.why: No Tier 1/2 document reviewed names which crucible makers buy Spruce Pine HPQ from Sibelco or The Quartz Corp, or which wafer makers buy those crucibles. Sibelco says only that its IOTA HPQ goes into CZ crucibles, and USGS does not name companies.
gaps.would_need: Crucible-maker annual reports (e.g., Shin-Etsu Quartz Products, Heraeus, Momentive/CoorsTek, Jiangsu Pacific Quartz), or supply agreements disclosed in filings.

gaps.topic: The Quartz Corp Drag, Norway processing and Spruce Pine site coordinates
gaps.why: USGS says at least one Spruce Pine HPQ producer sends product overseas for further processing, and TQC's registered office is in Drag, Norway. No page reviewed documents a Spruce Pine → Drag shipment or a processing facility address. Both Spruce Pine sites are mapped at city precision.
gaps.would_need: TQC annual accounts (Brønnøysund register) or a site page with facility addresses.

gaps.topic: Named polysilicon customers other than Siltronic
gaps.why: Only Siltronic's statutory report names its polysilicon supplier (Wacker). GlobalWafers says only 'top-tier global suppliers'. Wacker's Section 232 comment (BIS-2025-0028-0035) is redacted. Links from Wacker or Hemlock to Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, GlobalWafers or SK Siltron are therefore inferred.
gaps.would_need: SK Siltron DART business report supplier list, SUMCO/Shin-Etsu securities reports (yuho), Hemlock customer disclosures, or unredacted docket filings.

gaps.topic: Tokuyama and OCI polysilicon facilities (Shunan, Japan; OCI TerraSolar/Tokuyama JV in Sarawak, Malaysia)
gaps.why: Research was stopped for budget before Tokuyama/OCI primary documents were fetched. The companies are defined only from the SIA docket filing.
gaps.would_need: Tokuyama integrated report / yuho, and Tokuyama's 2025-07-09 JV notice (tokuyama.co.jp/eng/news/2025/2025070901.html).

gaps.topic: Gallium refiners outside China and U.S. high-purity gallium (New York facility)
gaps.why: USGS says one New York company refines high-purity gallium and that China produced 99% of primary low-purity gallium, but it does not name companies. The November 2025 DPA Title III $29.9M gallium/scandium award recipient (Louisiana) is also unnamed in USGS.
gaps.would_need: DoD/DoW award release or USAspending record for the DPA Title III gallium award; company pages for Japanese/other gallium refiners.

gaps.why: USGS MCS 2026 says rare-gas supply from Russia and Ukraine stayed limited because of the conflict, that 32% of U.S. neon went to semiconductors, and that U.S. neon net import reliance was about 52% in 2025. No facility-level Tier 1/2 source was retrieved for Ukrainian or other neon purifiers.
gaps.would_need: USGS Minerals Yearbook (rare gases), Linde/Air Liquide 10-K/URD disclosures, or company releases for neon purification plants.

gaps.why: USGS reports helium use for 'controlled atmospheres, fiber optics, and semiconductors' at 17% of U.S. use and lists import sources (Canada 47%, Qatar 28%), but no plant-level source was reviewed (e.g., ExxonMobil Shute Creek/LaBarge, Qatar Ras Laffan).
gaps.would_need: ExxonMobil 10-K, QatarEnergy reports, and industrial gas supplier filings naming fab helium supply.

gaps.topic: Tungsten, tantalum and cobalt facility-level sources
gaps.why: USGS MCS 2026 gives Tier 1 country data (China leads tungsten production and imposed export controls in February 2025; U.S. tantalum net import reliance is 100%). Facility-level documents (e.g., Almonty Sangdong, Global Tungsten & Powders Towanda, Global Advanced Metals Boyertown) were not retrieved before wrap-up.
gaps.would_need: Almonty SEC filings, Plansee/GTP and GAM site pages, and DPA Title III award records.

gaps.topic: Germanium downstream (GeCl4 to optical-fiber makers; Trail germanium to U.S. buyers)
gaps.why: Umicore Quapaw produces fiber-grade GeCl4 and Teck sells germanium from Trail into the U.S., but no document names the buyers (e.g., Corning). Corning's 10-K does not mention germanium.
gaps.would_need: Supply agreements or customer disclosures in Umicore/Teck/Corning filings.

gaps.why: USGS confirms HF is essential in semiconductor etching and cleaning, and Mexico is 64% of U.S. fluorspar imports, but no reviewed document links Orbia HF to electronic-grade HF producers (e.g., Stella Chemifa, Morita, Honeywell) or to fabs. The HF II plant capacity date is also undated.
gaps.would_need: Orbia annual report (BMV), Honeywell 10-K (Geismar HF), and electronic-grade HF producers' filings.
